doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Future of live performance and the rescheduled Hamilton gig
summary: Baron and Rowe speculate on audience trust, distancing in small halls, and their planned Hamilton concert.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do you have predictions about — let’s suppose and let’s hope that this pandemic fades away. What do you think is going to be the landscape for live performances in the future?

I think it’s going to take some time for people to really trust — although you know it’s funny because there’s an air in New York City, even though we’re walking around with masks on, there’s this sense, and spring is here, almost summer is here, that it’s all gone. You know? And like sometimes when I go to wash my hands for 20 seconds many times a day I say oh I can do 15 seconds it’s pretty cool. And no, you’ve got to do 20 seconds. I’m like washing the skin off my hands. I’m not doing it with the same exuberance I did three weeks ago but I’m still doing it. But the thoughts are like oh this is over. We have a little park near us and my wife and I walk there a couple of times a week, fully masked, and get a coffee or something. And you see people, a lot of people with masks, but a lot of people just sitting too close together. You know? And so I think it might just — the simple answer is I think it might be — well there’s two ways to look at it. There’s the people who want to be careful about putting a lot of people in chairs in a room, and then the people say come on let’s just do it. It’s over. You know.

Well it’s interesting you say that because you and I have a gig scheduled and I would love to be able to say yeah, get all your people in line, we’re going to do it. But even if — like we got some positive news regarding the fall semester and students coming back, but even then you may have students on campus but they may say something like no large gatherings, in a concert hall everybody has to sit like six seats apart or something. Those things are going to be dealt with and it’s very hard to predict.
Is — I’ve forgot already, where we’ll perform, is it the same place that the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band played?
So that’s not a very large space.
It’s not that large a space but maybe other arrangements could be made but we’ll see. I’m saying on tape that if we can’t do the fall then we’re going to do it sometime.
Bless you. So I don’t have to give the deposit back. Great. I love it.
But I could use a loan now that you did so well with unemployment.
Watch what you say, Baron. Well I appreciate that and I appreciate that it’s on tape. I would have trusted you even if it wasn’t on tape. You have a good reputation my man.
